title: Sky-Fever matchup draws 3.31M viewers, WNBA's largest regular-season audience in 29 years
dek: The Chicago Sky vs. Indiana Fever game on NBC and Peacock drew 3.31 million viewers, the highest regular-season audience in WNBA history since 1997. The broadcast included a courtside ejection of former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom late in the third quarter. Caitlin Clark finished with 37 points and 10 assists as the Fever won 113-90.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Sunday's Sky-Fever game drew 3.31 million viewers on NBC and Peacock, the most-watched WNBA regular-season game since the league's opening weekend in 1997.
bottom_line: The viewership figure marks a significant milestone for the WNBA amid expanded television coverage. The exact nature of the altercation between Freedom and Cloud remains unspecified in available reports, and the WNBA's specific eligibility criteria that exclude former NBA players are not detailed in the sourced material.
body:
Sunday's Chicago Sky versus Indiana Fever game drew 3.31 million viewers on NBC and Peacock, according to Nielsen Big Data + Panel and Adobe Analytics digital data reported by Front Office Sports. NBC confirms this is the most-watched WNBA regular-season game since the league's opening weekend in 1997.
The Fever won 113-90. Caitlin Clark finished with 37 points and 10 assists, while Kelsey Mitchell added 30 points, combining for 67 of Indiana's points, per Front Office Sports. The previous regular-season cable record was 2.6 million viewers for the August 16 Fever-Atlanta Dream game on ESPN, per the same report.
NBC is broadcasting WNBA games this season for the first time since 2002 as part of the league's new media rights deal worth more than 3 billion dollars, according to Front Office Sports. Fever-Sky games have consistently driven the highest WNBA viewership since 2024, when Clark and Angel Reese entered the league, the report notes. Reese was traded to the Atlanta Dream in April.
Late in the third quarter, former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Wintrust Arena after a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud, per Front Office Sports. Chicago has placed an indefinite ban on Freedom for attending Sky home games, the report states. According to league sources cited by Front Office Sports, Freedom is not banned from attending other WNBA games as a fan.
Kanter Freedom last played in the NBA in 2022, per Front Office Sports. The report notes that Freedom has been making statements about wanting to enter the 2027 draft as a woman. League sources told Front Office Sports that Kanter Freedom and former NBA player Royce White, who has also declared intentions for the WNBA draft, are not eligible to play in the league based on its current eligibility rules.
